name: Gerald G Wong
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager (CEO), Shanghai Cambridge Industries Group (CIG; SSE 603083 / HKEX 6166)
profile: Gerald G Wong (黄钢) founded CIG in 2005-06, a Shanghai maker of optical modules and broadband/wireless equipment; it listed in Shanghai in 2017 and added a Hong Kong listing. Demand for high-speed optical modules for AI data centers has driven CIG's recent growth. He has been chairman and CEO since 2011.
interesting_fact: Before he became an entrepreneur, Wong spent 1984-2000 at AT&T Bell Labs and rose to vice president at Lucent Technologies. He has over 40 years in telecom.
deep_cut_fact: Before CIG, he co-founded Photon Bridge (光桥科技(中国)有限公司) in 2000. He holds both a bachelor's and a master's in electrical engineering and computer science from MIT, both conferred in June 1985.
notes: Relevant to the data-center angle because CIG makes 800G/1.6T optical modules. The best route is the IR email or the board secretary office (board secretary: Jin Zeqing). Wong is a US/MIT-trained engineer, so outreach in English should work.

name: Marciano Testa
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder (chairman) of Agi / Agibank (NYSE: AGBK), Brazil
profile: Testa was born to a family of Italian immigrants in Rio Grande do Sul. In 1999, while still a college student, he started Agiplan as a credit distributor. It became a financeira in 2011 and a bank in 2016, when he bought Banco Gerador. Agibank serves underbanked Brazilians through a digital bank and in-person 'Smart Hubs'. It listed on the NYSE in February 2026, and he owns nearly two-thirds of it.
interesting_fact: He calls himself an 'empreendedor raiz' (grassroots entrepreneur). He began as a door-to-door 'vendedor pastinha' (briefcase salesman), selling credit to low-income people and retirees, and became a billionaire when Agibank listed on the NYSE.
deep_cut_fact: He started working at 8 to help his family. He opened his first business at 16 and sold it at 19, and calls that his 'primeiro MBA da vida real' (first real-life MBA). On legacy, he said he would like to be remembered as 'uma pessoa que transformou a própria história' (a person who transformed his own story).
notes: Glauber Correa has been Agi's CEO since 2021, and Testa sits on the board. Forbes' bio calls Testa 'founder, chairman and CEO', so his exact current title should be checked against the F-1 or 20-F. Some reports say he lives in the US. Press releases have also listed the agency address agibank@fsb.com.br as a press contact.

name: Yang Zehua
current_role: Former executive director and vice president, Baoxin Auto Group (now Grand Baoxin Auto Group, HKEX 1293); no current role found
profile: Yang Zehua (杨泽华) was a founding-family shareholder and executive director of Baoxin Auto Group, a BMW/luxury car dealer group based in Shanghai. It listed in Hong Kong in December 2011 in a HK$3.2bn IPO. At listing he held about 1.55bn shares; the controlling shareholder was Yang Aihua. China Grand Automotive bought control in 2015-16, and he stepped down as a director around 2016.
interesting_fact: Baoxin Auto's December 2011 Hong Kong IPO raised about HK$3.2 billion (US$414m), making it one of the larger Chinese car-dealer listings of that era.
notes: Very low public profile and last on the Hurun list in 2012. HKEX filings (e.g. https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2012/0314/ltn20120314214.pdf) list him as an executive director with Yang Aihua and Yang Hansong. MarketScreener gives Beihang (undergraduate) and a Dalian University of Technology MBA, but that is unverified. The family link to Yang Aihua is not confirmed. No published contact; probably not a good outreach target.

name: Fabricio Garcia
current_role: Vice President of Operations / Retail (physical stores and logistics), Magazine Luiza (B3: MGLU3); member of executive board
profile: Fabrício Bittar Garcia belongs to the founding family of Magazine Luiza (Magalu), the Brazilian retailer started in Franca in 1957. Forbes says he owned about 8% of the company in 2021, the year five family members joined its billionaires list. A career Magalu executive, he has run operations since 2020: physical stores, expansion, logistics and distribution. Since a 2025 reorganisation he runs 1P retail and logistics.
interesting_fact: In 2021 Garcia was one of five Trajano/Donato family members who joined the Forbes billionaires list together, after Magalu's e-commerce shift (about 69% of revenue) earned it the nickname 'the Amazon of Brazil'.
deep_cut_fact: Despite being family, he started at the bottom of the business. Garcia joined Magalu's commercial department in 1996 and worked up through purchasing roles, including a senior purchasing post in 2006-09, before becoming operations VP.
notes: Low public profile operating executive. His title comes from 2020-2025 reports (most recently a March 2025 restructuring), so check it on the IR site. Forbes calls him a grandson of founders Luiza Trajano Donato and Pelegrino Donato, but some sources say the founder had no children. Avoid stating the exact family relationship. Best route is Magalu IR or corporate communications.

name: Wu Yonghua
current_role: Executive Director and Co-CEO, ANTA Sports Products (HKEX: 2020), focused on FILA and internationalisation
profile: Wu Yonghua (吴永华) joined ANTA in October 2003 and spent two decades in sales and marketing at the Fujian-based sportswear group. He ran its Performance Sports brand group from 2019. In 2023 he became Co-CEO, overseeing FILA and ANTA's international expansion. His wealth comes from his long-held ANTA shares.
interesting_fact: In the 2023 management reshuffle (he was 52 at the time), Wu was given FILA and the group's further internationalisation, as ANTA grew into one of the world's largest sportswear groups. It also owns stakes in Amer Sports (Salomon, Arc'teryx, Wilson).
notes: The SEC insider tag (Alibaba CEO) is a name mix-up with Alibaba's Eddie Wu Yongming and is not this person. He has a very low personal media profile, so the best route is ANTA IR or its agency CDR. No sourced deep-cut fact was found.

name: Cynthia Paul
current_role: Founder, CEO and Chief Investment Officer, Lynrock Lake LP; director of Yext, ON24 and Allot
profile: Cynthia L. Paul spent 2002-2017 as a portfolio manager at Soros Fund Management, covering corporate credit, convertibles and equities. In 2017-18 she founded Lynrock Lake, a value-oriented fund that invests across the capital structure of technology, media and telecom companies. It holds large stakes in Teradata, Yext and ON24 (about 17.5%), and she sits on the boards of several of these companies.
interesting_fact: She is an activist-style tech investor. Lynrock reached a 2026 cooperation agreement with Teradata, and Yext appointed her to its board in July 2026. She has over 24 years of investing in public enterprise software companies.
deep_cut_fact: She chaired the board of semiconductor company Conexant Systems from 2013 to 2017, while still at Soros. She began her career in 1994 as head of convertible research at J.P. Morgan, after graduating from Princeton.
notes: A private investor with no personal website, press office or published email found. Lynrock Lake's address appears in SEC 13D/13G filings on EDGAR. Approach would have to go through a warm introduction or the board/IR offices of Yext, ON24 or Allot. The data-center/enterprise software angle (Teradata) fits the podcast. A MarketScreener page mentioning a Cribl CFO of the same name is a different person.

name: Zhang Guanfu
current_role: Founder and former chairman/controlling shareholder of Guizhou Xinbang Pharmaceutical (信邦制药, SZSE 002390); left as chairman in August 2016
profile: Zhang Guanfu (张观福), a pharmacist by training, founded Guizhou Xinbang Pharmaceutical in Guiyang and ran it as chairman and general manager from 1995. He took it public in Shenzhen in 2010, and it grew into a drug maker plus hospital and pharma-distribution group. He stepped down as chairman in August 2016 and sold down his shares. No public role since has been found.
interesting_fact: Before he became an entrepreneur, he was a government pharmacist-researcher. He worked at the Guizhou Provincial Institute of Traditional Chinese Medicine and the Guizhou Pharmaceutical Administration Bureau before founding Xinbang.
deep_cut_fact: He has a pharmacy degree from Guizhou Medical University and later took an MBA/EMBA at CEIBS (China Europe International Business School).
notes: Last on the Hurun list in 2021 and very low profile since leaving Xinbang in 2016. The SZSE filings on his share reductions (e.g. https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk01/finalpage/2016-07-12/080ea94f-c6d2-49a6-9154-e366833b5f2f.PDF) confirm he was the controlling shareholder. No personal contact was found, and the company IR is unlikely to forward messages now that he has left.

name: Zhang Yingjiu
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder (about 12.6% in 2025), Yangling Metron New Material (美畅股份, SZSE 300861); professor, School of Physics and Engineering, Zhengzhou University
profile: Zhang Yingjiu (张迎九, b. 1969) co-founded Yangling Metron in Shaanxi in 2015 with Wu Ying and others. Metron makes the electroplated diamond wire used to slice silicon wafers for solar panels and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2020. He was its second-largest shareholder, and his stake drove his Hurun ranking in 2020-21. He also left the company's board.
interesting_fact: Metron's diamond wire is an unglamorous but critical input to the solar boom. It is used to saw polysilicon ingots into the thin wafers in most of the world's PV panels.
deep_cut_fact: He is a serving physics professor at Zhengzhou University's School of Physics and Engineering. Metron's prospectus credits the 'Jia Haibo and Zhang Yingjiu team' with being first in the industry to launch multi-wire diamond-wire production equipment ('one machine, six wires'), which raised output per machine.
notes: A scientist-investor who gives almost no interviews. In 2025 he disclosed plans to sell part of his stake (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202505201676133954_1.pdf). Relevant to the energy/solar angle. Possible routes are the Metron board secretary office or his Zhengzhou University faculty page, but no published personal email was found.

name: Hu Yuhang
current_role: Vice Chairman, 37 Interactive Entertainment (三七互娱, SZSE 002555); long-time President of 37 Games (R&D arm)
profile: Hu Yuhang (胡宇航, b. 1976) is a co-founder of 37 Interactive Entertainment, one of China's biggest mobile/web game publishers (titles such as 'Puzzles & Survival' and 'Douluo Dalu' games). He has run its R&D brand 37 Games since 2013. His stake rose to 7% in 2020, and he was re-elected to the board in 2025 as vice chairman.
interesting_fact: He is the developer-side co-founder, leading 37 Games' studios while the group grew into one of China's top game exporters. In 2019 he was named a 'Craftsman Spirit Figure of the Game Industry' (游戏行业匠心精神人物).
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from Lanzhou University in China's northwest, far from 37's Guangzhou base, and later took an EMBA at Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business (CKGSB).
notes: He is low profile in English-language media. In December 2025 regulators (CSRC/SZSE) penalised several 37 Interactive directors, including him, over a 2018 related-party disclosure (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202512051794542444_1.pdf); avoid that topic. Best route is 37 Interactive IR or the board secretary (Wang Sijie).

name: Pan Hui
current_role: Long-time major individual shareholder of Sichuan Kelun Pharmaceutical (科伦药业, SZSE 002422); no executive role found
profile: Pan Hui (潘慧) was an early, large individual shareholder of Kelun Pharmaceutical, the Chengdu-based infusion-solution and drug maker controlled by founder Liu Gexin. In 2019 she was Kelun's second-largest shareholder with about 10.6%. Her holding has since fallen to under 5% (4.84% in 2022), and she has left the Hurun list.
interesting_fact: Kelun grew from a small Sichuan IV-fluid maker into China's largest infusion producer. It has since spun off Kelun-Biotech, which licensed antibody-drug conjugates to Merck.
notes: A passive shareholder with no public persona, interviews or biography found. Part of her stake was transferred to a Ya'an state asset company by court enforcement in 2020 (https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk02/finalpage/2020-02-15/fd85a7c9-6e44-4346-9b48-3dd0fc757bbb.PDF); avoid this topic. Not a viable outreach target; there is no route except via Kelun's board secretary.

name: Wang Yaolin
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, InventisBio (益方生物, SSE STAR 688382), Shanghai
profile: Yaolin Wang (王耀林, b. 1963), a US-trained pharmacologist, spent 18 years as a drug-discovery scientist at Schering-Plough and Merck. In 2015 he left to build InventisBio in Shanghai with other returnee PhDs. The company developed the targeted cancer drugs befotertinib (EGFR) and garsorasib (KRAS G12C), both out-licensed, and listed on the STAR Market in July 2022.
interesting_fact: InventisBio's KRAS G12C inhibitor garsorasib (格索雷塞) targets a cancer mutation long considered 'undruggable'. It reached approval in China, putting this ex-Merck lab scientist's startup among the few groups with a drug against that target.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his pharmacology PhD at SUNY Stony Brook and did postdoctoral research at Baylor College of Medicine in 1992-97. He then worked as a principal scientist at Schering-Plough (1997-2009) and Merck (2009-15), and only founded his company at 52.
notes: He is a US citizen with Chinese permanent residency and comfortable in English, having spent 20+ years in US pharma. Co-controllers are Jiang Yueheng (board secretary) and Dai Xing. Best route is ir@inventisbio.com. A 2019 Endpoints News article covers his decision to leave Merck (https://endpts.com/?p=60394).

name: Yang Weixin
current_role: Chairman and co-controlling shareholder (about 18.3%), Bros Eastern Co. (百隆东方, SSE 601339), Ningbo
profile: Yang Weixin (杨卫新) has chaired Bros Eastern since 2004, which he controls with his brother and vice chairman Yang Weiguo. Based in Ningbo, it is one of China's leading makers of 'colour-spun' (melange) cotton yarn, where fibres are dyed before spinning. He also served as general manager in 2015-2020 and 2024-2025.
interesting_fact: Bros Eastern moved early to Southeast Asia. Its Vietnam subsidiary now accounts for about 78% of the company's total capacity, which makes this Ningbo yarn group effectively a Vietnam-based manufacturer.
notes: A low-profile textile industrialist; no interviews or personal biography found. He also chairs Bros Group Ltd and family property companies in Ningbo. The energy-intensive spinning and dyeing operations in Vietnam could be a hook for the energy angle. The best route is the board secretary email.
